summary: Tested M2-S04 (validation, built by metadata-builder). Ran both declared checkers verbatim from the build directory exactly as the plan wrote them: check_validation_rules.py at the plan's declared build scope (--manifest-dir artefacts), which now scans two validation rules (M2-S03's and this step's) and printed 'Scanned 2 validation rule(s) across 2 file(s); 1 finding(s) detected.' with one REVIEW-severity advisory on this step's rule ('picklist logic has no explicit blank guard') -- exit 0, exactly as the step's own inputs.note predicted before this run; and check_products_and_pricebooks.py at step scope (--manifest-dir artefacts/M2-S04), which exited 0 with 'No issues found.' This run independently re-ran that same command against a freshly created, genuinely empty directory outside the build tree and got the byte-identical output and exit code, confirming the builder's own prior control-run finding -- recorded honestly as an exit 0 with nothing demonstrably asserted about this step's artefact, not as a positive validation of the catalog side of the rule. Also ran the always-on xml parse (2/2 files), the always-on manifest consistency check (ValidationRule named explicitly in package.xml with a file behind it, both directions consistent, no wildcard), and check-outputs --hashes (ok, nothing missing/empty/malformed). All four runnable tests passed. The step's one manual acceptance test was checked against the Given/When/Then shape (all three clauses present, Then directly inspectable) and deferred verbatim to the M2 milestone gate rather than ticked; as a courtesy this run also read deploy-order.md against both Then clauses without ticking them, and both hold -- section 2.1 names the dry-run settlement for the HasOpportunityLineItem formula-context claim, section 2.2 states 'forward gate only' for the re-firing-after-deletion conflict. results.json written with "passed": true and artefact_hashes from check-outputs --hashes; M2-S04 moved built -> tested via build_plan.py set-status.
confidence_rationale: Every declared test ran (or was correctly classified as manual), both always-on checks completed, and every result came from an exit code this agent observed directly -- the Step 7 HIGH row in agents/step-tester/AGENT.md. No command test was refused, no manifest exclusion had to be applied (none was needed: ValidationRule plainly has a standalone file), and check-outputs reported ok with nothing missing, empty or malformed. The products-and-pricebooks checker's unproven exit 0 does not itself trigger the MEDIUM row (that row is keyed to a refused command test, a coverage-gap manifest exclusion, or a check-outputs problem, none of which occurred) -- it is reported as a Process Observation instead of a confidence downgrade, per this run's instruction to record it honestly rather than read it as a pass on the catalog side of the rule.

process_observations.observation: check_validation_rules.py exited 0 at the plan's declared build scope and its output changed exactly as predicted once a second rule entered the tree -- from M2-S03's prior 'Scanned 1 validation rule(s)... 0 finding(s)' to this run's 'Scanned 2 validation rule(s)... 1 finding(s)', with the one new finding matching the step's own inputs.note prediction verbatim. This is a checker that proved something about the whole tree, not merely a green exit repeated by coincidence.

check_products_and_pricebooks.py's declared test on this step exits 0 with 'No issues found.' -- the checker was added to this step by amend-step --add-checker on 2026-09-18 to close a section 5 coverage warning (the step cites admin/products-and-pricebooks in skills[]), but a validation-rule step has no Product2, Pricebook2 or PricebookEntry metadata for it to inspect. This run independently confirmed the builder's own control-run finding: the identical command against a genuinely empty directory prints the byte-identical 'No issues found.' at exit 0. The exit 0 satisfies the declared 'expected: exit 0' and is recorded as a pass, but a reader of a green test list should not infer the rule's product-catalog correctness was checked here.

This agent's own Mandatory Reads (agents/step-tester/AGENT.md, 'What the tester judges for itself' item 3) cites skills/devops/metadata-api-coverage-gaps as documenting 'the component types that legitimately have no standalone file or no manifest member.' Reading that skill in full during this run found no such enumerated list -- its content covers Metadata Coverage Report support status (Metadata API / source tracking / unlocked packages / 2GP), a different question from which types lack a standalone source file for a manifest-vs-file check. This did not change the manifest verdict on this step (ValidationRule plainly has a standalone file, so no exclusion question arose), but the citation itself does not deliver what the playbook says it does, which would matter on a future step involving a genuinely file-less type.

set-status's own full-plan validate pass printed 19 pre-existing WARNs about other steps (M1, M3, M4) shipping a cited skill's checker with no declared acceptance test for it. None name M2-S04 or its cited skills (admin/validation-rules, admin/products-and-pricebooks); they predate this run and are outside this invocation's one-step scope, so nothing was changed on their account. This is the same 19-line set M2-S03's test run observed 19 minutes earlier, confirming no new WARN was introduced by this step.
